$comment: Rules the ESLint layers enforce at error that the oxlint layers do not.
`oxlint-parity.mjs` fails on any rule missing from oxlint that is absent here,
so every drop is a deliberate, reviewed entry. Measured against oxlint 1.78.0.
`layer` is the ESLint layer the rule is at error in. `native` names the oxlint
rule id when one exists but we still do not enable it. `replacement` records
the intended migration path for each gap.
A `frontend/*` key with a `rules` list records a partial gap: the rules still run,
but not on every file they ran on under ESLint. The parity check compares a union
across sample files, so it cannot see these, and it does not read these entries.

no-octal.reason: No oxlint rule. Largely covered incidentally: the oxc parser rejects legacy `0`-prefixed octal literals in strict-mode and module code, which is all of our source.
no-octal.replacement: No action unless non-module source becomes supported.

typescript/prefer-optional-chain.reason: Native but `nursery`, and it diverges. It reports `typeof crypto !== 'undefined' && crypto.randomUUID` in @n8n/crdt where ESLint does not, and its fix is wrong: `crypto?.randomUUID` still throws a ReferenceError when the global is undeclared, which is what the typeof guard prevents.
typescript/prefer-optional-chain.impact: Re-evaluate when the rule leaves nursery.
typescript/prefer-optional-chain.replacement: Re-evaluate after the rule leaves nursery and its undeclared-global fix is corrected.

import/export.reason: Native but `nursery`. Not enabling a pre-release rule silently; no divergence observed yet.
import/export.impact: Re-evaluate when the rule leaves nursery.
import/export.replacement: Enable after the rule leaves nursery and parity remains clean.

import/no-duplicates.reason: Oxlint reports separate type and value imports that import-x accepts in n8n-nodes-base.
import/no-duplicates.impact: The package keeps import-x/no-duplicates in its residual ESLint pass.
import/no-duplicates.replacement: Enable the native rule when its type-import behavior matches import-x.

no-self-assign.reason: Oxlint reports assignments in n8n-nodes-base that ESLint accepts.
no-self-assign.impact: The package keeps no-self-assign in its residual ESLint pass.
no-self-assign.replacement: Enable the native rule after its diagnostics match ESLint.

no-unsafe-optional-chaining.reason: Oxlint reports optional-chain expressions in n8n-nodes-base that ESLint accepts.
no-unsafe-optional-chaining.impact: The package keeps no-unsafe-optional-chaining in its residual ESLint pass.
no-unsafe-optional-chaining.replacement: Enable the native rule after its diagnostics match ESLint.

n8n-nodes-base/node-filename-against-con.reason: The JS-plugin bridge supplies different filename context and reports valid supporting files in n8n-nodes-base.
n8n-nodes-base/node-filename-against-con.impact: The package keeps this rule in its residual ESLint pass.
n8n-nodes-base/node-filename-against-con.replacement: Move the rule after Oxlint supplies the same filename context as ESLint.

typescript/consistent-type-imports.reason: oxlint's rule has no `emitDecoratorMetadata` carve-out. typescript-eslint goes silent in any file containing a decorator when `experimentalDecorators` + `emitDecoratorMetadata` are set, because converting such an import to `import type` erases the `design:paramtypes` metadata that DI resolves. oxlint reads no compiler options in this rule and offers no option to declare them, so it reported 3488 false positives across packages/cli/src, all in decorated files. Its fixer also fights n8n-local-rules/no-type-only-import-in-di: one adds `type`, the other removes it, so `oxlint --fix` does not converge.
typescript/consistent-type-imports.impact: Low at runtime. The direction that breaks DI stays guarded by no-type-only-import-in-di, and these packages leave `verbatimModuleSyntax` off, so TypeScript elides a type-only-used import at emit. The cost is drift from a clean baseline. The frontend layer enables the rule, because no frontend package uses decorators.
typescript/consistent-type-imports.replacement: Wait for the upstream emitDecoratorMetadata option, or use an approved shim that suppresses decorated files.

frontend/no-restricted-syntax.reason: editor-ui used package-specific AST selectors for its workflow-store and modal-key ratchets. They were `off`, and Oxlint has no `no-restricted-syntax` rule, so the move to Oxlint dropped them. The selectors are in the git history of `packages/frontend/editor-ui/eslint.config.mjs`.
frontend/no-restricted-syntax.impact: None now: no ratchet was on.
frontend/no-restricted-syntax.replacement: Write a focused rule for each selector before you turn its ratchet on.

frontend/vue-template-rules.reason: Vize lints the other template rules. Vize 0.715.0 maps these two, but reports nothing on fixtures that ESLint reports. They are not turned on, so that the Vize config does not claim coverage it lacks. Measured with Oxlint 1.78.0 and Vize 0.715.0.
frontend/vue-template-rules.impact: An invalid attribute name, or a `<template>` root that is empty or has `src` and content, is not reported by a linter.
frontend/vue-template-rules.replacement: Turn them on in `@n8n/oxlint-config/vize` when a Vize release reports them. See `OXLINT_MIGRATION_BLOCKERS.md`, "Raise the Vize pin".

vue/valid-attribute-name.reason: See `frontend/vue-template-rules`: Vize maps the rule, but reports nothing.
vue/valid-attribute-name.impact: An invalid attribute name, or a `<template>` root that is empty or has `src` and content, is not reported by a linter.
vue/valid-attribute-name.replacement: Turn them on in `@n8n/oxlint-config/vize` when a Vize release reports them. See `OXLINT_MIGRATION_BLOCKERS.md`, "Raise the Vize pin".

vue/valid-template-root.reason: See `frontend/vue-template-rules`: Vize maps the rule, but reports nothing.
vue/valid-template-root.impact: An invalid attribute name, or a `<template>` root that is empty or has `src` and content, is not reported by a linter.
vue/valid-template-root.replacement: Turn them on in `@n8n/oxlint-config/vize` when a Vize release reports them. See `OXLINT_MIGRATION_BLOCKERS.md`, "Raise the Vize pin".

vue/multi-word-component-names.reason: ESLint enforced this rule only on `defineComponent` objects in `.ts` files: it is `warn` or `off` for `.vue`. Vize lints `.vue` files only, and Oxlint has no native rule. Measured with Oxlint 1.78.0 and Vize 0.715.0.
vue/multi-word-component-names.impact: Component objects in `.ts` files, most of them test stubs, are not checked for this rule.

vue/no-mutating-props.reason: ESLint enforced this rule only on `defineComponent` objects in `.ts` files: it is `warn` or `off` for `.vue`. Vize lints `.vue` files only, and Oxlint has no native rule. Measured with Oxlint 1.78.0 and Vize 0.715.0.
vue/no-mutating-props.impact: Component objects in `.ts` files, most of them test stubs, are not checked for this rule.

vue/no-v-text-v-html-on-component.reason: ESLint enforced this rule only on `defineComponent` objects in `.ts` files: it is `warn` or `off` for `.vue`. Vize lints `.vue` files only, and Oxlint has no native rule. Measured with Oxlint 1.78.0 and Vize 0.715.0.
vue/no-v-text-v-html-on-component.impact: Component objects in `.ts` files, most of them test stubs, are not checked for this rule.

no-dupe-args.reason: No Oxlint rule. ESLint enforced it in `.vue` script blocks only. Measured with Oxlint 1.78.0 and Vize 0.715.0.
no-dupe-args.impact: Near zero: duplicate parameter names are a syntax error in strict mode, and every SFC script is a module.

no-undef.reason: Native but `nursery` in Oxlint 1.78. With Vue's compiler macros declared as globals, it reports 5 false positives in 3 editor-ui SFCs that have both `<script>` and `<script setup>`, because Oxlint does not share scope between the two blocks. Measured with Oxlint 1.78.0 and Vize 0.715.0.
no-undef.impact: An undefined name in an SFC script is not reported by a linter. TypeScript (`vue-tsc`) still reports it.
no-undef.replacement: Enable the native rule when it leaves nursery and shares scope between the two script blocks.

@typescript-eslint/naming-convention.reason: No Oxlint rule. In the frontend, ESLint enforced it in `@n8n/design-system` `src/components/N8nFormInput/validators.ts` only.
@typescript-eslint/naming-convention.impact: Property naming in one file is not enforced.

frontend/sfc-type-aware-rules.reason: Oxlint's type-aware rules (tsgolint) skip `.vue` files. ESLint ran these rules on SFC `<script>` blocks through vue-eslint-parser and `projectService`. They still run on `.ts` files. editor-ui and the frontend modules that ran Oxlint first already lacked them on `.vue`. Measured with Oxlint 1.78.0 and Vize 0.715.0.
frontend/sfc-type-aware-rules.impact: Promise and type misuse in component scripts is not reported. `vue-tsc` still type-checks them.
frontend/sfc-type-aware-rules.replacement: Vize's `type/no-floating-promises` (`vize lint --type-aware`) covers one of them, when its false positives are fixed upstream.

frontend/no-direct-component-imports-tem.reason: Oxlint gives JS plugins no template AST, so `@n8n/design-system/no-direct-component-imports` sees only the script. The script half still runs.
frontend/no-direct-component-imports-tem.impact: An `<el-*>` or other banned tag in a template is not reported. A banned import still is.
frontend/no-direct-component-imports-tem.replacement: Read the template with `@vue/compiler-dom`, as `require-teleported-tooltip-in-dropdown` does.

frontend/scriptless-sfc-js-plugin-rules.reason: Oxlint 1.78 runs no JS plugin on a `.vue` file that has no `<script>` block. The rule reads the template with `@vue/compiler-dom` and runs on every other SFC.
frontend/scriptless-sfc-js-plugin-rules.impact: The 18 SFCs that have no `<script>` block are not checked for a non-teleported tooltip in a dropdown.
frontend/scriptless-sfc-js-plugin-rules.replacement: None planned. Add a `<script>` block to an SFC that needs the check.

frontend/vue-unused-imports.reason: Oxlint sees only the script block of an SFC, so an import that only the template uses reads as unused. Turned on for `.vue`, it gave 531 findings in the 7 frontend modules with `.vue` files, all of them false positives.
frontend/vue-unused-imports.impact: An unused import in an SFC script is not reported. It still is in `.ts` files. Vize's `vue/no-unused-components` reports a component that `<script setup>` imports and the template does not use.
frontend/vue-unused-imports.replacement: Turn it on for `.vue` when Oxlint gives JS plugins the template scope.

vue/no-deprecated-dollar-listeners-api.reason: ESLint ran this rule on every file, `.ts` included. Oxlint has no native rule. Vize runs it as `script/no-deprecated-dollar-listeners-api`, but the lint scripts pass only `src/**/*.vue` to `vize lint`. Vize 0.715.0 also reports it in `.ts` files (probe).
vue/no-deprecated-dollar-listeners-api.impact: Composables and `defineComponent` objects in `.ts` files are not checked for this rule. SFC scripts still are.
vue/no-deprecated-dollar-listeners-api.replacement: Pass `.ts` files to `vize lint` as well, after a run that shows no false positives.
